(1) VCCs can be targeted by immune effectors and pharmacologic compounds; and (2) the targeting of VCCs by immune effectors or pharmacologic compounds can be used to deplete HIV-1-infected macrophages in vitro.

the VCC-associated HIV reservoir can be modulated by a variety of immunologic and pharmacological interventions, at least in in vitro models, thus suggesting that the same interventions could be effective in reducing this viral reservoir in vivo.
HIV-1-infected macrophages are a major source of virus production and that the HIV-1 reservoirs can be modulated by immunologic and/or pharmacologic agents.

the development of novel immunologic and pharmacological approaches for targeting HIV-1-infected macrophages and their VCCs in order to eradicate or curtail the macrophage associated viral reservoir in vivo.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

The main takeaway from our work is that
VCCs are dynamic and heterogeneous compartments that can be modulated by immunological and pharmacological agents.

the VCCs in infected macrophages are a potential therapeutic target for the development of anti-HIV-1 agents that could reduce viral reservoirs and improve the clinical management of infected patients.
